title: Petro Closes Foreign Agenda With Symbolic Final Trip to Cuba
detail: Gustavo Petro made his last official trip as president to Havana, Cuba, from July 31 to August 1 — closing his foreign agenda in Cuba rather than Washington as originally planned. Petro was received by Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel at the Palace of the Revolution, publicly opposed what he called US threats of military intervention against the island, and met Colombian students at ELAM, an institution linked to the 2016 FARC peace accord. The choice of destination carried heavy symbolism: President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella had already announced plans to sever diplomatic ties with Cuba starting August 7, making Petro's visit a final gesture underscoring his foreign-policy legacy before leaving office.

media.caption: Petro visits Havana on his final foreign trip as president
